subject: Feature prioritization: Lumen Health audit/export + residency guarantees
messages:
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: irene_choi@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Lumen: ask to prioritize audit-export + residency guarantees for close

Team —

Lumen Health is at the finish line for a multi-year contract (attached SOW_v2). They have two blocking asks that are gating signature and a production start in Jan:

1) Scheduled audit export of PII-scoped events to their S3 (daily CSV + on-demand full export) for audit reviews. They need predictable retention and a certified extract format.
2) Residency guarantee / tenant affinity for their production workload (US-west only) for data locality and compliance.

The commercial team has put a firm timeline on this: legal needs the export assurance and residency language in the SOW by EOD Friday (2027-11-05) to meet procurement windows. If we miss this, they will likely push to a competitor and delay the deal by a quarter.

Ask: can Product/Eng evaluate feasibility and provide a one-page tradeoff (ETA, ops impact, risk, and a minimum viable deliverable) by EOD Thursday so we can commit a staged approach in the SOW? I included a matrix of the audit fields Lumen expects (audit_requirements_matrix.xlsx) and the current redline contract.

Budget context: they are comfortable with a one-time implementation fee + a small uplift on committed monthly spend if we can guarantee residency and an export SLA.

Thanks — please flag any immediate blockers.

- Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2027 12:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Lumen: ask to prioritize audit-export + residency guarantees for close

Karthik —

Thanks for the context and attachments. A few clarifying questions before we commit to scope:

- Export format: is Lumen OK with NDJSON lines compressed (gz) instead of CSV for the daily export? That simplifies schema evolution.
- Export window: do they need a retention-cutoff for historical data backfills or only going-forward?
- Residency: do they require a hard guarantee (i.e., no cross-region failover) or an operational affinity where failover is permitted after N minutes?

Engineering constraints to surface: full production residency with zero cross-region failover has availability tradeoffs and will require dedicated node affinity (ENG-7312). The audit export can be built as a streaming ETL to S3, but we need clear acceptance criteria for field-level redaction and PII handling.

If we can get answers to the bullets above, we can draft a tradeoff doc and an estimated sprint plan.

- Irene
Irene Choi
Product Manager, Redwood Console

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: irene_choi@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2027 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Lumen: ask to prioritize audit-export + residency guarantees for close

Irene — answers inline:

- Format: Lumen legal prefers CSV for auditors, but they can accept NDJSON if we provide a small tool to convert to CSV; they emphasized "auditor-friendly" format. Prefer CSV.
- Backfills: yes, they want a one-time historical export for the last 24 months of relevant events (estimated 120GB compressed). They will accept a one-week window for the backfill to run.
- Residency guarantee: they want an explicit clause that production traffic remains in US-west region and that any cross-region failover is a documented, manual process requiring mutual sign-off. They understand risk but insist on contractual language.

Commercial levers: they will sign at our standard ARR + 10% uplift for commit, or we can negotiate a one-time engineering fee to cover the quota. Procurement has requested the redline by EOD Friday.

I attached the redline_contract_20271101.docx and the SOW. HubSpot link is here for the deal record: https://hubspot.company/contacts/DEAL-4821

Karthik

From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 03 Nov 2027 10:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Lumen: ask to prioritize audit-export + residency guarantees for close

Thanks — high level engineering response:

1) Audit export
- MVP: daily CSV export + on-demand full export endpoint. We can stream to their S3 with a small transform layer that enforces field ordering and redaction. Implementation estimate: 3 engineer-weeks (one backend + 0.5 infra) if we build on the existing export pipeline. Backfill for 24 months at ~120GB: one-off job, estimate 5 engineer-days to run and validate.
- Risks: schema drift, auth to external S3, and throughput limits for backfills. We'll need a contract-approved SLA for export availability (we can offer 99.5% for the export job, not 99.99% continuous).

2) Residency / tenant affinity
- Hard guarantee (no automatic cross-region failover) is viable but implies we must provision capacity in US-west dedicated to their workload and opt them out of cross-region autoscaling. This is operationally heavier and requires a reserved pool + routing rule — estimate 4 engineer-weeks to provision and instrument.
- Alternative: we can provide affinity with automatic failover only under defined conditions (catastrophic region outage), which reduces engineering time to ~1.5 engineer-weeks but will not satisfy their current legal language.

Given timelines, a staged approach seems reasonable:
A) Ship export MVP + backfill (3w + 5d) — low risk and closes most legal asks.
B) Commit to residency affinity with a documented runbook as interim approach (1.5w).
C) If they insist on hard contractual residency, we require a dedicated capacity commitment and additional procurement (4w).

We need Product to pick acceptance criteria and which staged approach we commit to in the SOW.

- Markus
Markus Klein
Director, Serving Runtime Engineering

From: monica_patel@redwood.com
To: irene_choi@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 04 Nov 2027 08:33:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Lumen: ask to prioritize audit-export + residency guarantees for close

Team — appreciate the quick estimates. To be explicit on business impact: this is a $1.8M ARR deal with multi-year references and a potential channel relationship with their group. Procurement has pushed hard: they must see "export capability" AND "residency language" in the SOW to approve vendor scorecards next week.

Proposal (to unblock legal and buy us time):
- We commit to A) Export MVP + backfill (deliverable: daily CSV export, on-demand full export, field-level redaction; deliver by Dec 15) AND B) Residency affinity runbook (interim, manual failover) to be documented and accepted by Lumen — deliver by Dec 31.
- In the SOW we will include a 90-day roadmap that calls out engineering follow-up for a contractual hard-residency SLA (with estimated cost and delivery window).
- Commercial concession: 10% uplift on committed ARR + one-time $40k engineering implementation fee to prioritize the work.

Ask to Product/Eng: can we sign up for the staged approach above? If yes, I will push this language into the SOW redline and get a procurement commitment. If no, we need a written alternative (and I need it by EOD Friday so procurement can review).

Monica
Monica Patel
Director, Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: monica_patel@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 04 Nov 2027 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Lumen: ask to prioritize audit-export + residency guarantees for close

Monica / Markus — good plan. Product accepts the staged approach with the following acceptance criteria so Legal/Procurement can get the SOW language:

Export MVP (Deliver by 2027-12-15):
- Daily export to Lumen S3 as CSV, gzipped, with a consistent field schema (fields documented).
- On-demand full export endpoint that kicks off backfill job; backfill window max 7 days to complete for 24 months of data.
- Field-level redaction rules applied at export time; sample export validation by Lumen (3 validation runs).
- Export availability SLA: 99.5% monthly for export job orchestration (not ingestion).

Residency affinity (Interim deliverable by 2027-12-31):
- Documented runbook showing US-west routing affinity, monitoring, and a manual failover runbook signed off by Ops.
- Telemetry hooks to verify traffic residency for the first 30 days post-cutover.

Product requests two things from Eng: a) a sprint slot in December for the export work (ENG-7312) and b) an owner for the backfill job + a runbook reviewer.

Markus — please confirm sprint availability and we will finalize SOW language. Once Eng confirms, Monica — go ahead and include the staged language and the commercial concession in the redline; procurement wants the draft by Friday EOD.

- Irene
Irene Choi
Product Manager, Redwood Console
